items.title: The oil market should brace for a forever stalemate in Iran
paras: The Iran–United States conflict has now endured about 250 days, keeping global crude prices above one hundred dollars a barrel. Oil traders expect a renewed round of hostilities after the upcoming United States midterm elections.

items.title: North Korean workers sold into Russia then stripped of wages, report finds
paras: The network is allegedly run by Moscow-based businessman Vladimir Sokolov (left). ( Supplied: GRC )
Russian brokers are advertising North Korean workers to companies as part of a forced labour program, a new report has alleged.
It found those involved are working up to 12 hours a day, six to seven times a week, and forfeiting most of their income to the North Korea's authoritarian regime.
The report found some North Korean workers were being sent to "facilities essential to Russia's war economy".
North Korean workers are being advertised online as for sale to Russian businesses as part of a forced labour program, a new report has found.
The workers' wages are being used to fund North Korea's ballistic missile program, and their labour is boosting the Kremlin's war economy, it alleges.

International human rights group Global Rights Compliance (GRC) said it had members pose undercover as representatives of a prospective company as part of a nine-month investigation into a labour-brokering network run by a Russian businessman.
It found the broker network charges a commission of between 100,000 and 150,000 roubles ($1,765 to $2,650) per North Korean worker it places with a company.
North Korean workers in a garment factory that GRC believes to be in Chekhov. ( Supplied: GRC )
The group alleges the North Koreans then work up to 12 hours a day, six to seven times a week, and forfeit most of their income to the authoritarian regime.
It said the Russian brokers have "turned the supply of North Korean labour into an organised industry".
"It's shocking to me, the normalisation of slave labour conditions in Russia," the report's lead investigator, Dylan Carter, told the ABC.

It is the latest in a series of reports to investigate the use of labour from North Korea, in breach of a resolution from the United Nations Security Council, which requires member states to repatriate North Koreans earning money in their territory.

The Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team, an international coalition set up to report on violations of UN sanctions against North Korea, recently found North Korean overseas workers raised between $US450 million ($633 million) and $US800 million last year for the authoritarian state's nuclear weapons program.
It found there could be anywhere between 35,000 and 101,000 North Korean workers overseas, primarily in China and Russia.

North Korea has denied providing forced labour, although organisations, including the United Nations, have documented it. Russia has also denied violating UN resolutions on using North Korean workers, despite several reports documenting it.
The GRC report focuses on a brokering network allegedly run by Moscow-based businessman Vladimir Sokolov.
A website it links to him advertises "Industrial internships for students from the DPRK [North Korea] in Russia".
It found his brokering network places groups of at least 50 workers at companies and receives payments for each worker.
Vladimir Sokolov (centre left) with North Korean officials at an agricultural factory. ( Supplied: GRC )

Undercover GRC investigators were reportedly told by an operations manager working for Mr Sokolov that "North Korean workers enter Russia on student visas, are enrolled at colleges they never attend, and are placed within Russian companies".
A change in Russian migration law in 2020 allows foreign students to work while studying in the country.
"This arrangement avoids work authorisations prohibited under UN sanctions and places workers outside of the protections of Russian labour law," the report says.
The investigation also found the Russian companies must have an official audit visit from North Korean officials before workers are sent there.
"Taken together, the findings show that North Korean labour in Russia is the product of an organised system rather than informal, ad hoc, or isolated labour arrangements," the report found.

The report said there were other brokers bringing in North Koreans, but that Mr Sokolov "distinguishes his scheme" by arguing it is "lawful because the 'students' are undertaking 'work training' as part of their education".
The report authors said they approached Mr Sokolov for comment but did not receive a response.

Another businessman associated with the network denied the North Koreans were workers, saying they were students doing "practical training at production sites" and the payments were "academic scholarships".
He said there was no "forced labour network" and that the allegations were "unsubstantiated" and based on "speculation".
While the majority of North Korean overseas workers are believed to be in China, there has been a growing number going to Russia, as the two countries tighten ties .

The GRC said "economic pressures and demands of [the] Ukraine war" are adding to Russia's need to boost its workforce, and its report found North Korean workers were "being used in facilities essential to Russia's war economy".
Mr Carter said North Korean workers were detected at an aluminium manufacturing plant that had contracts with major defence suppliers.
The GRC also sourced photos of workers at a food manufacturer that produces dry rations for Russian soldiers.
North Korean workers at a Russian factory outside of Moscow that produces preserved foods and military rations. ( Supplied: GRC )
Mr Carter said the photos were from a dog food line, but it was believed the North Koreans were also working packaging the military rations, which came out of the same building.
The workers are paid a proper wage, but it is alleged up to 90 per cent of overseas workers' wages are forfeited to the North Korean regime, helping to fund its ballistic missiles program.
Mr Carter said when the workers arrived in Russia, they faced a "stark and depressing world" where they were monitored and controlled.
"These are arrangements that benefit the North Korean and Russian states very heavily at the cost of North Korean civilians who ultimately pay the price for their labour," he said.
The Russian businessman investigated in the report, Mr Sokolov, has recently been sanctioned by the European Union.

Just over two weeks ago, the Council of the EU added Mr Sokolov to a list of people and entities that are "responsible for supporting, promoting or facilitating activities" that contribute to North Korea's weapons programs and "violating and evading United Nations sanctions".
The sanctions include an asset freeze and a ban on travelling to the European Union.
Vladimir Sokolov's office door has a sign showing the Russian and DPRK flags with a handshake graphic. ( Supplied: GRC )

He was one of three individuals and two entities added to the list, which now runs to more than 100, as part of a focus on activities "linked to the growing military and economic cooperation between the DPRK [North Korea] and Russia".
The council has accused Mr Sokolov of "promoting and facilitating commercial and industrial cooperation projects" with North Korea.
The report's revelations come at a time of heightened tension between North and South Korea, and amid a fraying relationship between Seoul and Ukraine.
North Korea positioned artillery along the demilitarised zone this week, with barrels pointed towards South Korea.
A howitzer with text that translates to "Destroy the US imperialist aggressors, the sworn enemies of the Korean people!" seen along the border this week. ( Reuters: Kim Hong-Ji )
It comes after a mine blast in the area injured three South Korean soldiers. Seoul has called for an apology from Pyongyang, while the latter claimed the incident was fabricated.

As Russia and North Korea continue to tighten ties, Ukraine has been warning that more troops from the hermit kingdom could be sent to join the war and has called for more support from other nations in the region, including South Korea and Japan.
But its relationship with Seoul has come under strain, following a dispute over the release of information about two Nmeorth Korean prisoners of war.

South Korea has withdrawn eight diplomatic personnel from Ukraine since President Volodymyr Zelenskyy revealed the North Korean soldiers were transferred to South Korea after being captured while fighting for Russia, an arrangement Seoul said was meant to be confidential.

items.title: Rogue taxi drivers accused of exploiting passengers at Perth airport, casino
paras: WA's transport minister says operations are underway to catch non-compliant taxi drivers. ( Gary Rivett: ABC News )
WA's transport minister says compliance checks are being ramped up, targeting illegal taxi operators outside Perth Airport and elsewhere.
One legitimate driver says the illegal operators are finding a way around existing compliance checks.
Transport Minister Rita Saffioti says one driver was fined after investigators used digital card data, and other investigations are underway.

Western Australia's transport minister says compliance checks will be ramped up in an attempt to weed out "bad apples" operating taxis in Perth, with a focus on the airport and the Crown Casino complex.
Rita Saffioti said "secret shopper" style checks and compliance blitzes had already taken place four times this year, and at least one driver was handed a fine.
Investigations were carried out in collaboration with WA Police and Australian Federal Police outside Perth Airport and the Burswood entertainment precinct — home to Perth Stadium and Crown Casino.
Perth Airport is one of the areas authorities are targeting in the compliance blitz. ( ABC News: James Carmody )
Perth taxi driver Jonathan Masih told the ABC illegal operators had found workarounds for compliance checks.
"A lot of drivers disappeared then because they got a network, they just ring each other up and then they don't show up," he told 102.5 ABC Perth.
Mr Masih said illegal taxi drivers taking fares from outside major hubs was a form of wage theft.
Protecting the reputation of legitimate taxi drivers is one of the minister's motivations. ( ABC News: Keana Naughton )
"Some of them are posing as a taxi, the other ones they've got private cars and they're just asking the customer to jump in," he said.
"I've been telling the airport authorities, federal police, Department of Transport, minister's office, but nothing changes."
Mr Masih said he was worried about how illegal taxis would impact unknowing passengers.
"It's not really good for the customers, if there's an accident or anything bad happens there's going to be legal issues," he said.
Ms Saffioti said ensuring compliance was as much about protecting the reputation of legitimate drivers as it was stamping out "bad apples" in the industry.
"We want to make sure … all those hard-working taxi drivers continue to get clientele and aren't impacted by those that are abusing the system."
Transport Minister Rita Saffioti says there need to be consequences for people exploiting the system. ( ABC News: Keane Bourke )
"Now we're able to go through and check data and check charges made compared to distance travelled and we've found some people are abusing that system," Ms Saffioti said.
"As a result, there's already been one fine imposed by the court and a number of other investigations are underway."
Ms Saffioti said there were a number of checks being made including car roadworthiness, driver authorisation and company authorisation.
"We need to make sure that those who are exploiting the system or not obeying the rules are dealt with," she said.

Share A A A Forrestania Resources has moved to bolster its feedstock source for the company’s emerging gold production business in Western Australia, signing a binding ore purchase agreement with ASX-listed High-Tech Metals for up to 400,000 tonnes of gold-bearing ore.

The deal gives the company preferential access to ore from High-Tech’s Mt Fisher gold project for a maximum of 24 months, providing another supply of future mill feed for the company’s burgeoning hub-and-spoke processing strategy.

Forrestania Resources has secured an additional 400,000 tonnes of ore feed for its s Edna May gold plant (pictured), with first processing planned for December 2026. Under the agreement, ore will be purchased on commercial terms determined by its grade, metallurgical recovery and prevailing gold prices, less agreed treatment and processing charges. The delivery schedules and specific processing campaigns will be agreed between the two companies during the term of the agreement.

The deal represents a key step in Forrestania’s strategy to become a significant WA gold producer by leveraging its two processing hubs at Edna May and Lake Johnston. The company has been assembling a significant inventory of ore sources to feed its two hungry plants, building a global mineral resource inventory that now tops a whopping two million ounces.

Forrestania’s initial focus is on the restart of its Edna May gold project, with first ore processing targeted for December, while its second hub at Lake Johnston is slated for commissioning in early 2027. Ore from Mt Fisher will likely feed the 2.9-million-tonne-per-annum Edna May processing plant, which is significantly closer to the deposit than the 3.2Mtpa Lake Johnson facility.

Management says it is already executing on that strategy by hauling ore from its own Taipan deposit and, under a similar recent ore purchase agreement with Star Minerals, from the Tumblegum deposit to Edna May ahead of the restart. Potential feedstock for the plant also includes the recently acquired Tampia project, which holds a 223,300-ounce resource. In a neat piece of operational history, Tampa’s previous owner, Ramelius Resources, previously trucked ore from Tampa to the very same Edna May plant Forrestania now owns.

Other spokes in the growing wheel include a 285,700-ounce resource at its Lady Ada and Lady Magdalene deposits and the 212,400-ounce British Hill deposit, from which ore has already been stockpiled at the Lake Johnston plant ahead of its own restart.

Forrestania Resources executive chairman David Geraghty said: “The Ore Purchase Agreement with High-Tech Metals continues Forrestania’s strategy of establishing a portfolio of third-party ore opportunities around our processing hubs. As we progress towards the restart of the Edna May gold project, Forrestania is already executing on that strategy through the haulage of ore from our Taipan and Tumblegum deposits to Edna May ahead of first ore processing planned for December 2026.”

The agreement lands amid a strong Australian gold backdrop, with spot prices hovering around A$6000 an ounce. The broader Western Australian market is also seeing a renewed focus on processing hubs and third-party ore, with producers pursuing toll-treatment arrangements and nearby deposits to lift plant utilisation and increase production.

On the corporate front, Forrestania has set a firm deadline for its takeover of Zenith Minerals, declaring its now-unconditional offer, first lobbed on June 9, will close at 5pm (AWST) on November 12. The company has ruled out any further extensions unless legally compelled under section 624(2) of the Corporations Act 2001, which provides for an automatic extension in certain circumstances, effectively putting the clock on Zenith shareholders still weighing up their options.

With 62.04 per cent of Zenith already tucked under its belt, Forrestania appears to be firmly in the box seat as it hunts down the magic 90 per cent ownership mark needed to trigger compulsory acquisition. Getting there would hand the company full control of Zenith and its 675,000 ounces of gold resources, adding another important piece to the puzzle in its broader ambition to build a consolidated WA gold powerhouse.

With the clock ticking down to the planned December 2026 restart of the Edna May processing plant, Forrestania appears to be systematically assembling the key ingredients of a genuine gold production business. Securing multiple ore sources, both internal and external, is a well-trodden path for aspiring producers looking to de-risk their operations and maximise the value of their expensive processing infrastructure.

By locking in a substantial third-party ore source to complement its burgeoning two-million-ounce resource base, Forrestania is not only feeding the beast but also giving itself options. In a gold market where every ounce counts, a flexible and scalable supply chain could be the key that unlocks the door to the company becoming WA’s next successful gold producer.

items.title: Concern as Queensland port plans sea dump in coral spawning season
paras: Port operators say they must undertake dredging to maintain navigable depths for vessels. ( ABC News )
The Port of Townsville will begin dredging sediment from shipping channels, and dumping it at sea, within days of mass coral spawning.
It scheduled the dredging and dumping for early November when inshore reef corals are expected to have spawned.
The timing has concerned Magnetic Island residents as sediment can have a negative impact for weeks after spawning.
The Port of Townsville in north Queensland is planning to dump silt and sediment at sea within days of coral spawning.
The timing has residents of nearby Magnetic Island concerned that poor water quality will compromise local reef reproduction.
Corals simultaneously release egg and sperm bundles during spawning. ( Supplied: SCU/Peter Harrison )
James Cook University coral ecologist Andrew Baird said Queensland inshore reefs were expected to begin spawning within days.
"Coral spawning is a very important part of reef recovery," Professor Baird said.
"If reefs get disturbed, the main source of recovery will be sexual recruits from the coral spawning."
The Port of Townsville said it was planning not to dredge, due to coral spawning, until November 4.
It said it would then dump naturally occurring sediment build-up from shipping channels at sea 6 kilometres offshore of Magnetic Island's Florence Bay.
A drone image of sediment in waters off Magnetic Island in 2025. ( Supplied: Lawrence Scheele )
Diving instructor Chad Bertram, who lives and runs a scuba and snorkel business on the island, said dredge spoil muddied the local waters.
"Easterly winds and the currents that we do have generally brings [the spoil] to the shores of Magnetic Island and on our fringing reefs," he said.
"There are times we have to cancel for safety when there is visibility of next to nothing."
Chad Bertram is a dive instructor who lives and works on Magnetic Island. ( ABC News: Chloe Chomicki )
He said he feared that dredge spoil in the water, particularly during coral spawning, could have long-term implications for the reefs.
"I think anything we can do to minimise our human impact can only be a good thing, so concerned is an understatement."
The Magnetic Island Nature Care Association, led by Gethin Morgan, has spent years raising concern about the port dumping spoil at sea.
The port dumps sediment in a dredge material placement area (DMPA). ( Supplied: Port of Townsville )
The area in Cleveland Bay, between Townsville and Magnetic Island, is excised from the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park and has been an approved disposal site for decades.
"It is a real shock to hear that they are going to do dredging and dumping in the middle of the spawning season," Mr Morgan said.
"We all know that October and November are months in which corals spawn, and they can also be very windy months."
Australian Institute of Marine Science coral ecologist Katharina Fabricius said coral larvae were sensitive to poor water quality well after the initial spawning.
"They are looking for clean reef surfaces and that could be up to two weeks after the spawning event, sometimes longer," she said.
"During those times the larvae are searching for places that are free of sediment, then they settle and become baby corals.
"Any type of silt and sediment is affecting coral spawning, no matter where it comes from."
Katharina Fabricius is a coral ecologist with the Australian Institute of Marine Science. ( ABC News: Chloe Chomicki )
The Port of Townsville said it had voluntarily planned for no dredging during the main predicted spawning window in October as a precaution.
"Maintenance dredging of the port's main shipping channels and harbour is scheduled to recommence from November 4 for 10 days to remove naturally occurring sediment build-up," a spokesperson said.
"Maintenance dredging is an essential and routine activity that supports the safe movement of vessels, which is a statutory responsibility for the port.
"The dredging program is being undertaken some kilometres from sensitive coral reef habitats, and environmental modelling does not predict impacts on those reefs."
The spokesperson said the port had undertaken maintenance dredging and sea placement at this time of year previously, most recently in 2024.

Outside of tech and earnings, Wendy’s soared 15.1 per cent to $US7.09 after Trian Fund Management, run by investor Nelson Peltz, offered to buy the chain for $US7.35 per share in cash.

That helped offset a drop for Boston Scientific, which fell 5 per cent even though the seller of medical devices reported a milder drop in profit for the latest quarter than analysts expected. It gave a forecast for profit in the current quarter that fell short of analysts’ expectations.
Robinhood Markets sank 4.2 per cent after reporting weaker profit and revenue for the latest quarter than analysts expected.
In the bond market, Treasury yields ticked higher, and the yield on the 10-year Treasury rose to 5.03 per cent from 4.99 per cent late Tuesday.

It’s near the high end of its range since shooting upward from 3.97 per cent when the war with Iran sent oil prices and worries about inflation much higher. But it’s pulled back after topping 5.30 per cent earlier this month and touching its highest level since 2002.

Rising oil prices pushed upward on Treasury yields Wednesday as uncertainty continues about what will happen in the Middle East and the global energy industry. The price for a barrel of Brent crude, the international standard, climbed 2.7 per cent to $US112.39.
In stock markets abroad, South Korea’s Kospi jumped 6.6 per cent following SK Hynix’s leap. Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 1.1 per cent, while France’s CAC 40 rose 0.1 per cent.

items.title: Bathla offered top dollar for land, but some sellers fought to be paid
paras: Bathla Group bought a parcel in Box Hill from Michael Ryan for $39.5 million. It missed settlement dates, so Ryan financed part of the sale.

Legal records show Bathla, through subsidiaries, failed to secure funding on three separate property transactions totaling about $130 million. The delays, attributed to rapid expansion, left the company vulnerable when the market cooled, prompting court‑ordered payments. Sellers now face higher risks when buyers rely on external financing, potentially reshaping future property deals.
Keep an eye on court rulings that could tighten buyer financing protocols.

items.title: Bad inflation result lays bare the ugly truth: There is no easy way out
paras: Jim Chalmers and Anthony Albanese are caught in a political bind when it comes to inflation. ( ABC News: Matt Roberts )
It is hard to imagine after nearly five years of economic pain, but the grim truth revealed by yesterday's batch of high inflation numbers is inescapable: the worst is yet to come.

Most observers now think the Reserve Bank will hike rates again on Tuesday. That would take the cash rate to 4.85 per cent, its highest level in 18 years. By now, we know this means a tighter financial squeeze for all borrowers.

Few will want to spare a thought for the politicians, but the news also piled on the agony for Treasurer Jim Chalmers, who had to front up once again for a stony-faced press conference and a Question Time laden with jeers from the opposition benches.

As he has done countless times, Chalmers acknowledged those "doing it tough" and solemnly swore the government would continue to be "responsible". And, as always, he snarled at "commentators" who say public spending is the root cause of the problem.

He might have a point. The role of global events is obvious, and is pushing up inflation all over the world. And a private sector investment boom, propelled by the rush to build data centres, hasn't helped either. They're excuses, but they're real ones.
Still, how many times can you reassure people that you're doing everything you can and that you're sensitive to the difficulty they're enduring before your words lose weight?
The answer: you can keep it up for as long as you can sell hope. And that's getting tough.

Rewind to 2022, when this inflation episode began, and hope was a carefully calibrated part of the message. The government and the Reserve Bank were singing from the same song sheet, promising a relatively painless route out of trouble.

They called it "the narrow path to a soft landing". Interest rates would go up, but not as harshly as in other countries. They might stay high for a little longer, but without doing excessive damage to the jobs market or the broader economy in the process.
Was the plan to tackle inflation, supported by RBA governor Michele Bullock, too good to be true? ( ABC News: John Gunn )

There were always those who said this sounded too good to be true. Inflation has wrought havoc whenever it has taken hold in history, and it has rarely been possible to banish it without a recession, such as the one Paul Keating said we "had to have" in 1990.

But it was an admirable ambition, and it's not entirely anyone's fault that it didn't work out. Yes, the "narrow path" strategy probably was the reason why Australia had more heat left in inflation when the war hit. But that's why it was called "narrow".

And the war, coupled with the AI investment boom, have made for a perfect storm not just in Australia but in other countries, too. The boom pushed up demand, and the war constrained what could be supplied, stretching out the gap where inflation thrives.

That is the simple and ruthless logic of inflation. When demand in an economy outstrips what can be supplied, inflation is the result, because the excess demand has nowhere to go other than to bid prices up.

To stamp that out, all that can be done is to slash demand or expand our capacity for supply. The latter option is what economists mean when they talk about productivity. Sluggish productivity growth is what Michele Bullock calls our "fundamental challenge".

But, in the meantime, the only other option is to slash demand, from anywhere. Rate hikes do this by slugging borrowers. Critics who say they do not address the root cause of inflation misunderstand the aim; it might be unfair, but it can be effective.
Dealing with inflation will put further pressure on everyday households. ( ABC News: Tristan Hooft )
The government can also reduce demand, either by cutting spending or hiking taxes. These can be more targeted approaches, but the political difficulties are obvious.

That is why economists like Chris Richardson tend not to ask governments to slash and burn, and instead judge them by the precautionary principle: at the very least, don't make things worse by spending more or handing out large tax cuts.

Of course, that is exactly what governments are tempted to do when voters are worn down by all those high prices. And, as Chalmers put it on Tuesday, helping people with the cost of living can be legitimate and necessary. It's an exercise in "balance".

As the opposition has pointed out, the government could have been a little braver if it wanted to. Spending like the EV discount and the home batteries discount might have achieved a climate goal but has put billions into the pockets of high-income earners.

But these are small in the grand scheme of things. And as the government points out, nobody in politics wants to identify acceptable spending cuts on a grander scale. It's hard to argue that a subsidy here or there is the main reason we are where we are.

Anyway, that sort of quibbling dodges the ugly truth about what lies ahead. The Reserve Bank, with the government's support, tried to get rid of inflation without triggering job losses and a recession. The soft approach didn't work.

That means that narrow path, and that soft landing, are likely beyond us. We have escaped the worst until now, with minimal change in the jobs market and minimal business closures or distressed housing sales.
Absent a productivity boom, which nobody can clearly articulate how to create, we will be going harder for longer, suppressing demand well into 2027.

That will happen with higher rates, and it will probably happen on the budget balance sheet too. For all his defensiveness about the role of government spending, Chalmers has promised further savings and poured cold water on calls for cost-of-living relief.
Around the cabinet table and the RBA board table is a shared recognition: that inflation is destructive, that it is making people angry, but that the only way is through.

items.title: Ten things to look out for in the Budget
paras: It’s Budget day. The run-up to Andy Burnham and John Healey’s first fiscal event has been rather less eventful than last year. There’ve been no daily leaks, no pitch-rolling press conferences and no hysteria. Everything that’s trickled out to the papers over the last few days has been small beer.

So we have a mystery: will this Budget be trick, treat, both or neither? If what Healey unveils to the House of Commons just after 12.30 today proves small in terms of spending and revenue, the Treasury team will be briefing that this was prudence rather than boring. With economic growth tentatively coming back to life so far this year, and following two Reeves Budgets which hiked taxes by a record £75 billion, they know there is little room for anything big.

Healey’s overall aim is for his Budget to give ‘breathing space for businesses and households’. What that is likely to mean is small measures paid for by small tax rises on banks, bookies and big businesses. One such measure was already announced this morning: the scrapping of standing charges on gas bills. That will be paid for by increasing the unit charge on gas charges but it brings bills down because it rewards efficiency in gas usage. Expect more of that.
Otherwise here are ten things I’ll be watching out for in the Budget statement and the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR)’s report:

When Rachel Reeves sat down after last November’s Budget she was, rightly, chuffed at having doubled her fiscal headroom to £22 billion and reassured jittery markets. By this spring it had barely changed to £23.6 billion.

If you believe what has been widely speculated, or indeed The Spectator’s headroom tracker, increased government borrowing costs and expectations of interest rises have eroded it down to around £11 billion. If that proves true then will Healey use tax hikes and spending cuts to return it to more than £20 billion – or, as we’ve reported, might he think that a figure closer to £15 billion is enough?

The big surprise at the last Budget was that the ‘black hole’ never materialised and that headroom was a lot better than had been leaked. I think that could happen again. If it does it will be because wage growth and unemployment forecasts have been revised in a positive direction. Look out for them.

The other week the IMF gave Britain a pat on the back for being one of the only countries with serious plans to get rid of its deficit. But that assessment was based on tax and spending plans left by Rachel Reeves that no one considers credible. If they’re maintained they imply massive spending cuts right when the next election is due. Surely that’s not something any Labour government is actually going to deliver. If there is any extra money Healey will surely be tempted to address that.
Healey will also feel pressure to use any spare cash to get the ball rolling on defence spending given he resigned over our failure to do anything about reaching the new GDP target.

We already know one way Healey plans to increase defence spending is through capital investment in defence infrastructure. He hopes to achieve this while sticking to the fiscal rules. One wheeze that he will attempt to use are these so-called public financial institutions (PuFins) such as the national wealth fund and British business bank. The idea is that because the state takes on an asset as well as a liability then overall debt levels don’t change as judged by the rules. But I’m not convinced that’s true given that he’ll still need to go to the gilt markets for the initial outlay at a time when gilt yields remain very high.

I’ll of course have one eye on the gilt market. They’ll want to see credible plans that reduce borrowing but also tackle our baked-in inflation problem. If anything goes against that then Healey can expect an expensive reaction.

One leak we have had out of No. 11 is some sort of change to the income tax threshold so that the latest increase to the state pension does not drag pensioners whose sole income is the state pension into paying income tax. But how exactly will he achieve that? Will it be an age-based policy? Or a new threshold for everyone on low incomes?

The freezing of those thresholds has dragged lots more people – not just pensioners – into paying tax and they’ve dragged millions further up the tax bands too. These stealth taxes make up a huge part of the record high tax burden kicked off by the Tories and continued by this government. We’ll get new figures on just how much money that has raked in and how many of us it has affected.

The OBR has been repeatedly criticised for taking a too positive view of migration in terms of its fiscal costs and contributions. Will those assumptions be revised further today? Even if they’re not I expect a fall in their near-term forecasts for migration as the Boriswave reverses. That could also have an impact on headroom though it would likely improve GDP per capita.

The big economic surprise this year has been our GDP growth. The fastest in the G7 it has beaten most forecasts. Historically British growth tends to outperform in the first half of the year and then peter out as the year goes on. Do the OBR think that will happen again? Or, like the ONS, do they see the early shoots of AI boosting productivity and growth and what will that mean for their overall forecasts?

items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

items.title: Reserve Bank holds 36 th Conference of State Finance Secretaries
paras: The 36 th Conference of State Finance Secretaries was held on October 27, 2026 at RBI, Mumbai. The theme of the Conference was ‘Role of Quality of Expenditure, Effective Cash and Prudent Debt Management in Enhancing States’ Fiscal Sustainability’. The Conference was attended by the Finance Secretaries of 27 States and three Union Territories as well as senior officials from the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, Controller General of Accounts and the Comptroller and Auditor General of India. Governor, Reserve Bank of India inaugurated the Conference. Addressing the participants, the Governor emphasised the importance of maintaining the quality of expenditure to ensure the long-term fiscal health of the States. He also emphasised on the need for the States to adopt prudent borrowing strategies and efficient cash management practices. The Governor urged the States to onboard onto the Unified Lending Interface (ULI) and utilise Programmable Central Bank Digital Currency (P-CBDC) for Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT). He also advised States to make effective use of the State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC) forum. During the Conference, the Governor released a Booklet titled ‘Compendium on Cash and Debt Management for State Governments’. The Booklet summarises relevant concepts, operational processes and good cash and debt management practices in a concise and accessible format. The meeting reviewed, inter alia, market borrowings by the States, short-term financial accommodation to the States from Reserve Bank, adoption of Benchmark Issuance Strategy by the States, etc. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1395

items.title: "No shortage of oil in world and prices should hopefully come down", says Hardeep Singh Puri
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Hardeep Singh Puri, Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas on Tuesday said that there is no shortage of oil in the world and prices will come down soon, answering the question of the recent upswing in crude oil prices. Speaking to the media, the Union Minister cited global factors such as the war in the Middle East and voluntary cuts in oil production which are influencing the oil prices in the global market. He said, "It depends on global factors. One thing is very clear, there is no shortage of oil in the world...Today, more and more oil is coming on the market...There are other factors like geopolitical tensions. So, there is no shortage of oil but if there is tension in one part of the world, then the freight cost, and insurance freight cost will go up. Today, let us all hope that better sense prevails, that call for peace that our Prime Minister has been making from every forum...There is more than enough oil in the world and prices should hopefully come down. That's my expectation..." "If there's tension in one part of the world, then the cost of, if you have to take a longer route, then the cost of the freight cost, the insurance rate cost, that will go up...There's more than enough oil in the world, and prices should hopefully come down," he commented in his personal capacity.

The union minister said many countries such as Brazil, and Guayana among others are coming with their oil. Citing the stable prices in the last 3 years, the minister said that the government is taking every possible step to ensure stable oil prices. "Central government at every stage has stepped in to cushion and bring the prices down from November 2021 to May 2022. Now there are some global factors. The cost at the retail point is determined by the cost of the barrel in the international market plus the cost of transportation, freight, insurance, retailers, refining cost and margin, then dealers, margin, etc. We are solving all the problems we can, now you tell the global community to hold and bring them down," he added. This comes after oil prices rose nearly 2 per cent on Monday, reclaiming major losses from last week's sell-off. Brent crude features upped by $1.44, or 1.97 per cent in the afternoon. Earlier this month, Puri had said that the country is well-prepared to meet its growing energy demands, with a diverse range of oil sources. Speaking on the availability of oil in the global market, Puri emphasised that India has expanded its procurement base, moving from 27 suppliers to 39. (ANI)

items.title: Asia's Largest Mindfulness India Summit 2024 Marks a New Era for Corporate Culture and Personal Well-being with the Inau
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel PNN Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: The Mindfulness India Summit 2024, an initiative by the Mindful Science Centre, presented by HSBC and supported by CII Leadership and HR Committee, successfully concluded its two-day event on October 17 and 18, 2024, establishing new benchmarks in corporate culture and personal well-being. With over 40 international and national experts addressing mindfulness, emotional intelligence, and neuroscience, the summit highlighted how these principles are essential in transforming leadership, enhancing employee engagement, and fostering sustainable well-being within organizations. The evolving workplace landscape, particularly the increasing role of AI, requires a renewed focus on human-centric leadership and emotional resilience. The summit provided a platform for forward-thinking leaders to explore how mindfulness can effectively bridge this gap, ensuring both corporate excellence and employee well-being . The summit featured MasterChef Sanjeev Kapoor as the Chief Guest, who shared how mindful leadership has played a pivotal role in building his culinary empire. Along with Chris Ruane, Ex MP British Parliament and Chair of Mindfulness Initiative UK, J N Behl and Global Holistic Health Guru Mickey Mehta, Kapoor also launched Manish Behl's new book "Observe - 101 Mindfulness Practices", a guide designed to make mindfulness accessible for both professionals and individuals in their everyday lives. Behl, a global mindfulness expert and founder of the Mindful Science Centre, shared, "With this book, I want to demystify mindfulness and make it accessible to everyone. Mindfulness is not a complex or distant concept, but a practical tool for reducing stress, improving focus, and fostering deeper connections in both personal and professional settings." The Mindfulness India Summit 2024 has successfully proven that mindfulness is no longer a luxury but a necessity in modern corporate structures. By adopting mindfulness practices, organizations are not only creating more compassionate work environments but are also enhancing their overall performance and sustainability in a world increasingly shaped by technological and emotional complexity. The 2 days also saw the launch of Mindfulness Impact Awards, to honor organizations and individuals who have integrated mindfulness into their corporate structures and personal lives. These awards reflect the growing recognition that workplace culture directly affects employee productivity, creativity, and overall well-being. Manish Behl, founder of the awards, explained, "Corporate success today goes beyond profit; it's about fostering environments where employees thrive mentally, emotionally, and physically. Our vision with these awards is to inspire a deeper integration of mindfulness in corporate cultures worldwide. By recognizing these pioneers, we hope these awards inspire companies and individuals to further integrate mindfulness into their environments, ultimately fostering happier, more productive workplaces, communities, and a more compassionate world." The awards were designed to acknowledge champions of mindfulness across categories, recognizing those who incorporate mindful practices to improve workplace culture, employee engagement, and societal impact. Winners ranged from corporate giants like Aditya Birla Group and Accenture to global educators and community leaders. items.title: Mukka Proteins Limited Announces Rs 98 Crore Preferential Issue for Acquisition and Expansion
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel VMPL Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: Mukka Proteins Limited , India's largest fish meal and insect meal producer and a leader in the animal protein industry , has announced the approval of a preferential issue worth Rs 98 crore by its Board of Directors. This strategic move will help Mukka Proteins in its ongoing domestic and international acquisition and expansion efforts, reinforcing its position in the global market. A significant portion of the funding will come from the promoter and promoter group, underlining their commitment to the company's robust growth strategy. The preferential issue will comprise up to 1.96 crore equity shares at Rs50 per share, aggregating to Rs98 crore. This price includes a premium of Rs49 per share on the face value of Rs1. Mukka Proteins will use the raised capital to enhance production capabilities and meet the growing global demand for sustainable and high-quality protein solutions, particularly in the fishmeal and insect meal sectors. In a clear show of confidence, Mukka Proteins' promoters have committed to a capital infusion of INR 60 crore through a preferential allotment of equity shares. This significant financial backing will be used to strengthen the company's financial position, reduce debt, and fund key operational improvements. Mukka Proteins has consistently embraced sustainability, having commercialized insect protein as a significant innovation for the aquaculture and animal feed industry. The company's waste-to-food initiatives have contributed to environmental sustainability, particularly in collaboration with the Mangaluru municipality for waste management. These efforts not only align with global environmental best practices but also enhance circular economy processes, focusing on converting municipal waste into valuable protein and oil products. Mukka Proteins is known for its strong commitment to ecological preservation, evident through the development of sustainable products such as fishmeal, fish oil, and insect protein. As a key player in the aquaculture and nutraceutical markets, Mukka contributes 25-30% of the market share in India's fishmeal and fish oil industry. The company plans to expand its operations further, capitalizing on this capital infusion to enter new markets and enhance its global footprint.

This issuance is subject to necessary statutory and regulatory approvals, including shareholder approval at the upcoming Extra-Ordinary General Meeting (EGM) on November 16, 2024. Managing Director and CEO Harris commented, "This preferential issue is a major milestone for Mukka Proteins as we continue to strengthen our market position. Our growth plans remain firmly rooted in sustainability, and this capital will enable us to scale up production, diversify our product offerings, and reinforce our commitment to responsible and eco-friendly business practices." Mukka Proteins Limited is poised to capture new opportunities in the animal protein sector, reinforcing its legacy of innovation, sustainability, and operational excellence. Mukka Proteins Limited : Mukka Proteins Limited is a leading manufacturer and exporter of fish meal , fish oil, and other protein products. The company has built a reputation for delivering high-quality, sustainable protein products to a global customer base. With a commitment to innovation and quality, Mukka Proteins serves industries including aquaculture, pet food, and agriculture across multiple continents. Headquartered in Mangalore, India, Mukka Proteins operates state-of-the-art processing facilities that meet stringent international standards. The company is dedicated to sustainable practices and has been at the forefront of environmental stewardship within the protein processing industry. items.title: Hon’ble Prime Minister of India inaugurates the Reserve Bank of India’s Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute
paras: The Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, today inaugurated the Reserve Bank of India’s newly established Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. This marks a significant milestone in strengthening the technological foundation of India’s financial system. Hon’ble Governor of Odisha, Shri Brajmohan Ram, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Odisha, Shri Mohan Charan Majhi; Hon’ble Union Finance and Corporate Affairs Minister, Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman; Hon’ble Union Minister for Tribal Affairs, Shri Jual Oram; Hon’ble Deputy Chief Ministers of Odisha, Shri Kanak Vardhan Singh Deo and Smt. Pravati Parida, and Hon’ble Members of Parliament, Shri Manmohan Samal and Smt. Aparajita Sarangi, also graced the event. 2. In his address, the Hon’ble Prime Minister highlighted the significance of the institutions inaugurated today - the Data Centre and the Cybersecurity Training Institute - in strengthening India’s digital financial infrastructure and advancing its technological self-reliance. The PM described the facility as a reflection of India’s changing approach to governance focused on taking the benefits of economic development to every region and every citizen. He emphasised that a secure banking system needs secure digital infrastructure supported by robust data centres and powerful computing systems and RBI’s new Data Centre is a critical step in this direction. 3. In her address, the Hon’ble Union Minister of Finance and Corporate Affairs underscored the strategic importance of resilient infrastructure in safeguarding financial stability and supporting sustained economic growth. She further said that the new Data Centre will house RBI’s mission-critical systems, including RTGS and NEFT, while the Training Institute will build expertise in cybersecurity, AI and other emerging technologies. 4. In his welcome address, Reserve Bank Governor Shri Sanjay Malhotra expressed gratitude to the Hon’ble Prime Minister for his participation in the event. He emphasised the Reserve Bank’s commitment to leveraging emerging technologies, strengthening digital infrastructure, enhancing cybersecurity, developing indigenous technological capabilities and supporting the country’s aspiration to become a developed nation by 2047. 5. The event was attended by distinguished dignitaries from the Central Government, State Government, industry, academia, persons of eminence, Directors of the Central Board of the Reserve Bank, heads of banks, technology providers and senior officials of the Reserve Bank. items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: "C-295 facility represents work culture of New India," says PM Modi as he and Spanish PM inaugurate facility
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Vadodara (Gujarat) [ India ], October 28 (ANI): Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Monday inaugurated the TATA- Airbus aircraft assembly facility complex in Vadodara. The facility will manufacture C-295 aircraft at the TATA Advanced Systems Limited campus. PM Modi said that the C-295 facility represents the work culture of a new India . "Recently, we lost the country's great son Ratan Tata ji. If he had been among us today, he would have been happy, but wherever his soul is, he would be happy. This C-295 aircraft factory reflects the new work culture of New India ... When I was the Gujarat CM, it was decided to set up a factory in Vadodara to build train coaches. The factory was also prepared for production within a record time. Today, we are exporting the metro coaches manufactured in that factory to other countries. I am confident that in the future, the aircraft made in this factory will also be exported to other countries," PM Modi said. "Today the defence manufacturing ecosystem in India is touching new heights. If we had not taken concrete steps 10 years ago, it would have been impossible to reach this level today. At that time, no one could even imagine that there could be such large-scale defence manufacturing in India . But we decided to walk on the new path, set a new goal for ourselves. And today the result is before us," PM Modi added. The Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez underlined the importance of the new industrial site. Sanchez said, "Today we are not only officially inaugurating a cutting-edge industrial facility. Today we're also witnessing how an extraordinary project between two emblematic companies becomes a reality. Prime Minister Modi, this is another triumph of your vision. Your vision is to turn India into an industrial powerhouse and a magnet for investment and business. This partnership between Airbus and Tata will contribute to the progress of the India n aerospace industry and will open new doors for the arrival of other European companies." " Tata is probably the best exponent of India n industrial strength. Its products and services are present in virtually every country on the planet. Tata is a giant among giants. As for Airbus , it embodies the very essence of a united Europe. Committed to technological innovation and the creation of jobs and prosperity. For my country, for Spain , being an integral part of the Airbus consortium, defending the values it represents. Values on which the very idea of Europe is based on cooperation, modernity and progress," Sanchez added. During the inauguration of the TATA Aircraft Complex for manufacturing C-295 aircraft, Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran announced the facility's goals. "The final aircraft assembly complex for the first aircraft to be delivered is being set up here. I must commit to our Prime Minister that exactly two years from now we will deliver the first indigenously manufactured aircraft and we will request and we'll work with your office to block the date so that you can come and inaugurate the facility and receive the first product. The first 200 engineers from Tata Group are already in Spain going through the training that is required, and we have worked with 40 SME companies and we will be adding more companies to build the entire localisation that is required for the product," he said. This collaboration between Tata Advanced Systems Ltd. (TASL) and Airbus Spain will mark India 's first private sector final assembly line (FAL) for military aircraft, boosting the nation's aerospace capabilities. The plant, located at TASL's Vadodara campus, is part of India 's Rs 2.5 billion deal signed in 2021 to acquire 56 C-295 military transport aircraft from Airbus . Under the agreement, Airbus will deliver 16 aircraft directly from Spain , while the remaining 40 will be manufactured in India by TASL. This project will create a comprehensive ecosystem for aircraft development, covering assembly, testing, certification, and maintenance throughout the lifecycle of the aircraft. Major India n defence players like Bharat Electronics Ltd (BEL) and Bharat Dynamics Ltd (BDL), along with smaller enterprises, are also contributing to this project. The C-295 aircraft will strengthen India 's Air Force fleet with a modern and more reliable transport solution. Earlier in the day, PM Modi and Sanchez participated in a roadshow in Vadodara as they headed to inaugurate Tata Advanced Systems Ltd's facility. (ANI)

items.title: "India matters most for future of planet" says British High Commissioner Lindy Cameron
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): In recent times when climate change has become a pressing issue with countries across the world being ravaged due to climate catastrophes, it becomes imperative to discuss and deliberate upon global actions that can help the world rise up and meet these challenges. At the NDTV World Summit's a discussion was held on the theme, "India Matters The Most For Future Of Planet". Participants in the discussion included Erik Solheim, Former Minister of Climate and the Environment of Norway; Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India; Shishir Priyadarshi, President Chintan Research Foundation; Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative. "India is the country that matters the most for the future of the planet and climate change. India's ambition for development should not in any way be constrained by the responsibilities of the planet," Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India, emphasised. She noted that the UK is committed towards the Multilateral Development Banks (MDB) reforms, technology and research support in India to aid the efforts. "Every dollar invested in resilient infrastructure pays 4 times over," said Cameron. "Lived experience of climate emergencies helps people to understand why their government needs to take policy action now," she added. Further talking about the need for urgent government action, Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative said, "Series of disasters affecting both developed and developing countries are serving as a wake-up call. As rich countries will get more and more affected by climate change which they did not imagine till a couple of years ago, most vulnerable countries are going to be struggling with impacts who also have very less capacity to deal with it. India is taking a leadership role in the global fight against climate change. Initiatives such as Global Biofuels Alliance, International Solar Alliance, and Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure are some efforts taken by India in recent years to manage the climate crisis. (ANI)

items.title: India sends humanitarian aid to Palestine; consignment comprises 30 tons of essential items
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, India took a significant step in providing humanitarian aid for the people of Palestine. This initial consignment comprises 30 tons of essential items, including medicines, surgical supplies, dental products, general medical items, and high-energy biscuits, which will be distributed through the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA). Sharing a post on X, Randhir Jaiswal, the official spokesperson of the Ministry of External Affairs wrote, "India sends humanitarian assistance for the people of Palestine through UNRWA." "The first tranche of assistance comprising 30 tons of medicine and food items has departed today. The consignment includes a wide range of essential medicines and surgical supplies, dental products, general medical items and high-energy biscuits," the post added.

Notably, a few days ago, the World Food Programme issued a warning for northern Gaza, saying that WFP's supplies are depleting. Sharing a post on X on October 12, WFP wrote, "Escalating violence in northern #Gaza is having a disastrous impact on food security. No food aid has entered the north since 1 October. It is unclear how long WFP's remaining food supplies in the north, already distributed to shelters and health facilities, will last." Earlier on October 20, the United Nations renewed its call for an end to the war in Gaza, emphasising the urgent need for the release of hostages, the cessation of the displacement of Palestinians, and the unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid. In a statement released by the UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, Tor Wennesland, the UN expressed deep concern, stating, "The nightmare in Gaza is intensifying. Horrifying scenes are unfolding in the northern Strip amidst conflict, relentless Israeli strikes and an ever-worsening humanitarian crisis." Last month, UNRWA had said people in Gaza are living in "inhumane" conditions. The agency said on the social media platform X that piles of waste are accumulating in central Gaza, while sewage water is leaking into the streets. The UN agency called for an immediate ceasefire. (ANI)

items.title: "Trust but verify...," says former envoy KP Fabian on patrolling agreement between India-China along LAC
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): KP Fabian , former India n Ambassador to Canada, struck a cautious note regarding the recent agreement between India and China on border patrolling along the Line of Actual Control ( LAC ), advising that while trust is essential, verification is equally important. While speaking with ANI, he said, "It's a very important statement that says that India and China have come to an agreement about normal patrolling and that there will be disengagement. The Foreign Secretary says that we are now looking at the resolution of the problem which arose in 2020." He added, "Some years ago, before a meeting, PM Narendra Modi was going to China for another international meeting. It (the issues) were resolved. But, let us recall that the Chinese did not carry out (the solution). The agreement was in two stages. In the first stage, India will withdraw first, then China will withdraw. That was done. In the second stage, China had to withdraw first, and then India , which they didn't do. Then, they constructed a lot of things. So, this step is welcome. Let me put it this way, trust but verify." The former diplomat further said that being neighbours, it is necessary for India and China to have "good neighbourly relations" if possible.

He said, " China is coming under a lot of pressure from the West. Americans are saying that China has been supporting Russia (with regard to the Russia-Ukraine conflict). Chinese electric vehicles are coming under high tariffs and so China is coming under pressure... And I believe that China and India , both being big countries but neighbours, it is necessary to have, if possible, good neighbourly relations." On Monday, Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri, said India and China have reached an agreement on the patrolling arrangements along LAC . The agreement was reached ahead of the BRICS Summit which will be attended by PM Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping . "On several areas along the Line of Actual Control , we held discussions with Chinese interlocutors, both on diplomatic as well as the military levels through meeting with military commanders at various levels. These discussions had in the past resulted in the resolution of standoffs at various locations. There are some locations and areas where stand-offs had not been resolved," said Misri. "Now, as a result of the discussions taking place over the last several weeks, an agreement has been arrived at on patrolling arrangements along the LAC in the India - China border areas. This is leading to disengagement and eventually a resolution of the issues that had arisen in these areas in 2020," he added. (ANI)
